```{r setup}
# posterior predictive checks (density overlay and mean), by group if given
custom_ppc <- function(fit, group = NULL, ndraws = 100) {
  pal <- scale_fill_viridis_d(begin = 0.3, end = 0.8, alpha = 0.5, option = "mako")
  if (!is.null(group) && group %in% names(fit$data)) {
    p <- list(pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "dens_overlay_grouped", group = group),
              pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "stat_grouped", stat = "mean", group = group))
  } else {
    p <- list(pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "dens_overlay"),
              pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "stat", stat = "mean"))
  }
  plot_grid(plotlist = lapply(p, function(x) x + pal + theme_classic()), ncol = 2)
}

ci <- function(x, digits = 2) paste0(round(median(x), digits), " [95% UI: ",
                                      round(quantile(x, 0.025), digits), "–",
                                      round(quantile(x, 0.975), digits), "]")
```

# Purpose {.unnumbered}

- Test whether the vocalizations of the focal bellbird are classified more often as the sympatric species it could have imitated than as their allopatric relatives, and more often than the vocalizations of other bellbirds
- Test whether the classifications of the focal bellbird changed over time

Classifications come from the cross-validated BirdNET classifiers of the [model fitting](birdnet_model_fitting.qmd) report. The fits are saved in `data/processed/cv_fits/`.

# Cross-validated classifiers

## Design

- All training and test clips were pooled and split into 5 folds grouped by recording (all clips of a recording in the same fold) and stratified by species, seed 123
- For each fold, the classifiers were trained on the other 4 folds (early stopping on a random 20% of the training clips) and classified the held-out fold, so every clip has a prediction from a model that never heard its recording
- Training and classification used a 400–12,000 Hz bandpass
- 33 hyperparameter configurations were compared (3 chosen by hand and 30 drawn at random from the search space of BirdNET-Analyzer's built-in tuner); for each classifier, the simplest configuration within one standard error of the highest out-of-fold macro-averaged AUPRC was selected (rule set before seeing the results, without using the focal bellbird). See the [model fitting](birdnet_model_fitting.qmd) report
- Per-species thresholds maximize F1 on the out-of-fold predictions. A clip is assigned to its highest-confidence species if it reaches that species' threshold, otherwise it is unassigned
- The focal bellbird clips are classified by the 5 fold models of the selected configuration: confidences are averaged across models (ensemble) and the out-of-fold thresholds are applied

```{r selected configurations}
folds <- read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "folds.csv"))
best_cfg <- with(read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "selected_configurations.csv")), setNames(config, model))[models]
data.frame(Classifier = model_labels[models], `Selected configuration` = best_cfg, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
```

## Selected classifiers

Out-of-fold performance by species of the selected configurations.

```{r selected classifiers}
oof <- lapply(setNames(models, models), function(m)
    read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, paste0("oof_predictions_", m, ".csv")), check.names = FALSE))
thr <- lapply(setNames(models, models), function(m) optimal_thresholds(oof[[m]], model_spp[[m]]))
focal_pred <- lapply(setNames(models, models), function(m)
    read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, paste0("focal_predictions_", m, ".csv")), check.names = FALSE))

per_sp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) {
    r <- cv_metrics(oof[[m]], model_spp[[m]], thr[[m]])$per_species
    data.frame(Classifier = paste0(model_labels[[m]], " (", best_cfg[[m]], ")"), r)
}))
names(per_sp) <- c("Classifier", "Species", "Precision", "Recall", "F1", "AUPRC", "Threshold", "Clips")
kable(per_sp, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

In the sympatric + allopatric classifier the aracaris and the oropendolas are the weakest classes, each confused mostly with its close relative. Out-of-fold confusion matrices (proportion of the clips of each species; numbers are clips):

```{r oof confusion}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5

cm <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) {
    lv <- c(model_spp[[m]], "Unassigned")
    d <- as.data.frame(table(True = factor(oof[[m]]$true, levels = model_spp[[m]]),
                             Predicted = factor(oof[[m]]$predicted, levels = lv)))
    d$Proportion <- d$Freq / ave(d$Freq, d$True, FUN = sum)
    d$Classifier <- paste0(model_labels[[m]], " (", best_cfg[[m]], ")")
    d
}))
cm$Classifier <- factor(cm$Classifier, levels = unique(cm$Classifier))

ggplot(cm, aes(Predicted, True, fill = Proportion)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(Freq > 0, Freq, ""), color = Proportion > 0.5), size = 3.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "black"), guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, limits = c(0, 1)) +
    facet_wrap(~ Classifier, scales = "free") +
    labs(x = "Predicted", y = "Vocalizing species") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "italic"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), strip.background = element_blank())
```

# Sympatric and allopatric species

Is a heterospecific classification of the focal bellbird more often the sympatric species (a possible model) than its closely related allopatric relative (which it could never have heard)?

Other bellbirds are the out-of-fold predictions of all bellbird clips used to train the classifiers (`r sum(oof$sympatric_and_allopatric$true == "Procnias tricarunculatus")` clips). Each was classified by a model that never heard its recording.

```{r symp allo data}
est <- readRDS("./data/processed/extended_selection_table_sympatric_and_allopatric_species.RDS")
focal_meta <- data.frame(clip = est$sound.files, recording = attr(est, "check.res")$orig.sound.files)
focal_meta <- focal_meta[est$source == "mimic_bellbird", ]

recording_of <- function(clip) sub("\\.wav_[0-9]+$", "", clip)

build <- function(m) {
    fp <- focal_pred[[m]]
    op <- oof[[m]][oof[[m]]$true == "Procnias tricarunculatus", ]
    rbind(data.frame(clip = fp$clip, recording = focal_meta$recording[match(fp$clip, focal_meta$clip)],
                     predicted_sp = fp$predicted, vocalizing_type = "focal"),
          data.frame(clip = op$clip, recording = recording_of(op$clip),
                     predicted_sp = op$predicted, vocalizing_type = "others"))
}

bb_sa <- build("sympatric_and_allopatric")
bb_sa$vocalizing_type <- factor(bb_sa$vocalizing_type, levels = c("others", "focal"))

kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(`Classified as` = bb_sa$predicted_sp, bb_sa$vocalizing_type)))
```

```{r symp allo plot}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

het <- bb_sa[bb_sa$predicted_sp %in% c(heterosp_sympatric, allopatric_spp), ]
het$genus <- factor(sub(" .*", "", het$predicted_sp), levels = c("Pteroglossus", "Psarocolius", "Ramphastos"),
                    labels = c("Aracaris", "Oropendolas", "Toucans"))
het$type <- factor(ifelse(het$predicted_sp %in% allopatric_spp, "Allopatric", "Sympatric"),
                   levels = c("Sympatric", "Allopatric"))
het$bird <- factor(ifelse(het$vocalizing_type == "focal", "Focal bellbird", "Other bellbirds"),
                   levels = c("Other bellbirds", "Focal bellbird"))
n_bird <- table(bb_sa$vocalizing_type)
cnt <- as.data.frame(table(bird = het$bird, genus = het$genus, type = het$type))
cnt$Proportion <- cnt$Freq / as.numeric(n_bird[ifelse(cnt$bird == "Focal bellbird", "focal", "others")])

ggplot(cnt, aes(genus, Proportion, fill = type)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.75) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Freq), position = position_dodge(0.8), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ bird) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Sympatric = "#408AB4", Allopatric = "#7B4F9D")) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Vocalizations classified as", fill = NULL) +
    theme(strip.background = element_blank())
```

## Focal bellbird

The probability that a heterospecific classification of the focal bellbird is the sympatric species rather than the allopatric one (0.5 if both were equally likely by chance), with the recording as a random effect.

```{r symp allo focal model}
d1 <- bb_sa[bb_sa$predicted_sp %in% c(heterosp_sympatric, allopatric_spp), ]
d1$mimic_type <- as.integer(d1$predicted_sp %in% heterosp_sympatric)

priors1 <- c(prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = "Intercept"), prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"))

mod1 <- brm(mimic_type ~ 1 + (1 | recording), data = d1[d1$vocalizing_type == "focal", ],
            family = bernoulli(), prior = priors1, chains = chains, iter = iter, cores = cores,
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), seed = 123,
            file = file.path(fit_dir, "sympatric_allopatric_focal"), file_refit = "on_change")
```

```{r mod1 summary}
#| results: "asis"
#| fig-height: 3

extended_summary(mod1, n.posterior = 1000, fill = mako(10)[8], trace.palette = mako,
                 remove.intercepts = FALSE, highlight = TRUE, print.name = FALSE)
```

```{r mod1 ppc}
#| fig-height: 3

custom_ppc(mod1)
```

## Focal vs other bellbirds

With the out-of-fold predictions, `r sum(d1$vocalizing_type == "others")` clips of other bellbirds were classified as one of these species, which allows estimating the focal vs others contrast.

```{r symp allo contrast model}
priors1b <- c(prior(normal(0, 1.5), class = "Intercept"), prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b"),
              prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"))

mod1b <- brm(mimic_type ~ vocalizing_type + (1 | recording), data = d1,
             family = bernoulli(), prior = priors1b, chains = chains, iter = iter, cores = cores,
             control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), seed = 123,
             file = file.path(fit_dir, "sympatric_allopatric_focal_vs_others"), file_refit = "on_change")
```

```{r mod1b summary}
#| results: "asis"
#| fig-height: 3

extended_summary(mod1b, n.posterior = 1000, fill = mako(10)[8], trace.palette = mako,
                 remove.intercepts = FALSE, highlight = TRUE, print.name = FALSE)
```

```{r mod1b ppc}
#| fig-height: 3

custom_ppc(mod1b, group = "vocalizing_type")
```

```{r mod1 estimates}
p_focal1 <- plogis(as_draws_df(mod1)$b_Intercept)
ratio_focal1 <- p_focal1 / (1 - p_focal1)

post1b <- as_draws_df(mod1b)
p_others1b <- plogis(post1b$b_Intercept)
p_focal1b <- plogis(post1b$b_Intercept + post1b$b_vocalizing_typefocal)
or1b <- exp(post1b$b_vocalizing_typefocal)
```

::: {.alert .alert-info}

#### Summary

- When a focal bellbird vocalization was classified as a heterospecific, it was the sympatric species with probability `r ci(p_focal1)`, i.e. `r ci(ratio_focal1, 1)` times more often than its allopatric relative (`r sum(d1$vocalizing_type == "focal" & d1$mimic_type == 1)` vs `r sum(d1$vocalizing_type == "focal" & d1$mimic_type == 0)` clips)

- Other bellbirds were rarely classified as any of these species (`r sum(d1$vocalizing_type == "others")` of `r sum(bb_sa$vocalizing_type == "others")` clips; `r sum(d1$vocalizing_type == "others" & d1$mimic_type == 1)` sympatric). Probability that such a classification is the sympatric species: other bellbirds `r ci(p_others1b)`, focal bellbird `r ci(p_focal1b)`; odds ratio focal vs others `r ci(or1b, 1)`

:::

# Only sympatric species

Is the focal bellbird classified as a heterospecific (instead of its own species) more often than other bellbirds? Unassigned clips are excluded.

```{r symp data}
bb_s <- build("sympatric")
bb_s$vocalizing_type <- factor(bb_s$vocalizing_type, levels = c("others", "focal"))
kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(`Classified as` = bb_s$predicted_sp, bb_s$vocalizing_type)))

d2 <- bb_s[bb_s$predicted_sp != "Unassigned", ]
d2$prediction_type <- as.integer(d2$predicted_sp != "Procnias tricarunculatus")
```

```{r symp model}
priors2 <- c(prior(normal(-3, 1), class = "Intercept"), prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b"),
             prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"))

mod2 <- brm(prediction_type ~ vocalizing_type + (1 | recording), data = d2,
            family = bernoulli(), prior = priors2, chains = chains, iter = iter, cores = cores,
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999, max_treedepth = 15), seed = 123,
            file = file.path(fit_dir, "sympatric_only"), file_refit = "on_change")
```

```{r mod2 summary}
#| results: "asis"
#| fig-height: 3

extended_summary(mod2, n.posterior = 1000, fill = mako(10)[8], trace.palette = mako,
                 remove.intercepts = FALSE, highlight = TRUE, print.name = FALSE)
```

```{r mod2 ppc}
#| fig-height: 3

custom_ppc(mod2, group = "vocalizing_type")
```

```{r mod2 estimates}
post2 <- as_draws_df(mod2)
or2 <- exp(post2$b_vocalizing_typefocal)
p_focal2 <- as.numeric(posterior_epred(mod2, newdata = data.frame(vocalizing_type = "focal", recording = NA), re_formula = NA))
p_others2 <- as.numeric(posterior_epred(mod2, newdata = data.frame(vocalizing_type = "others", recording = NA), re_formula = NA))
```

::: {.alert .alert-info}

#### Summary

- `r sum(d2$vocalizing_type == "focal" & d2$prediction_type == 1)` of `r sum(d2$vocalizing_type == "focal")` assigned focal bellbird vocalizations were classified as a sympatric model species (predicted probability `r ci(p_focal2)`), against `r sum(d2$vocalizing_type == "others" & d2$prediction_type == 1)` of `r sum(d2$vocalizing_type == "others")` vocalizations of other bellbirds (`r ci(p_others2, 3)`)
- Odds ratio focal vs other bellbirds: `r ci(or2, 0)`

:::

# Mimicry through time

Daily proportions of the focal bellbird vocalizations assigned to each category by the cross-validated sympatric-only classifier. Montezuma Oropendola (`r sum(focal_pred$sympatric$predicted == "Psarocolius montezuma")` clips) is not modeled. Clips below their species' threshold are unassigned.

```{r time data}
rec_info <- read.table("./data/raw/Recording_dates_.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ";")
rec_info$date <- gsub("/", "-", rec_info$date)
rec_info$date <- gsub("out", "ago", rec_info$date)
rec_info$date <- gsub("set", "sep", rec_info$date)
rec_info$date <- as.Date(rec_info$date, format = "%d-%b-%y")

fp <- focal_pred$sympatric
fp$recording <- focal_meta$recording[match(fp$clip, focal_meta$clip)]
fp$date <- rec_info$date[match(fp$recording, rec_info$sound.files)]
cat(sum(is.na(fp$date)), "clips without a recording date\n")
fp <- fp[!is.na(fp$date), ]

cats <- c("Procnias tricarunculatus", "Pteroglossus torquatus", "Ramphastos sulfuratus", "Unassigned")
dat <- as.data.frame(table(date = fp$date, pred = factor(fp$predicted, levels = c(cats, "Psarocolius montezuma"))))
names(dat)[3] <- "n"
dat$date <- as.Date(as.character(dat$date))
dat$total <- ave(dat$n, dat$date, FUN = sum)
dat <- dat[dat$pred %in% cats, ]
dat$prop <- dat$n / dat$total
dat$pred_common_name <- factor(common_names[as.character(dat$pred)], levels = common_names[cats])
dat$julian_day <- as.numeric(format(dat$date, "%j"))
dat$obs <- factor(seq_len(nrow(dat)))

kable(aggregate(n ~ pred_common_name, dat, sum), col.names = c("Category", "Clips"))
```

Binomial model: Julian day with intercepts and slopes varying by category, and an observation-level random effect for overdispersion.

```{r time model}
priors3 <- c(prior(normal(0, 2.5), class = "Intercept"), prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"),
             prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"))

mod3 <- brm(n | trials(total) ~ scale(julian_day) + (1 + scale(julian_day) | pred_common_name) + (1 | obs),
            family = binomial, data = dat, prior = priors3, chains = chains, cores = cores, iter = iter,
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99), seed = 123,
            file = file.path(fit_dir, "mimicry_through_time"), file_refit = "on_change")
```

```{r mod3 summary}
#| results: "asis"
#| fig-height: 3

extended_summary(mod3, n.posterior = 1000, fill = mako(10)[8], trace.palette = mako,
                 remove.intercepts = FALSE, highlight = TRUE, print.name = FALSE)
```

```{r mod3 ppc}
#| fig-height: 3

custom_ppc(mod3)
```

Slope of each category (log-odds per SD of Julian day):

```{r slopes}
slopes <- function(fit) {
    post <- as.data.frame(fit)
    cols <- grep("^r_pred_common_name\\[.*,scalejulian_day\\]$", names(post), value = TRUE)
    s <- sapply(cols, function(cl) post$b_scalejulian_day + post[[cl]])
    colnames(s) <- gsub("\\.", " ", sub("r_pred_common_name\\[(.*),scalejulian_day\\]", "\\1", cols))
    data.frame(Category = colnames(s), Slope = colMeans(s),
               `2.5%` = apply(s, 2, quantile, 0.025), `97.5%` = apply(s, 2, quantile, 0.975),
               check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}
sl3 <- slopes(mod3)
kable(sl3, digits = 3)
```

```{r time plot}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

nd <- expand.grid(julian_day = seq(min(dat$julian_day), max(dat$julian_day), length.out = 100),
                  pred_common_name = levels(dat$pred_common_name), total = 100)
nd$fit_prop <- colMeans(posterior_epred(mod3, newdata = nd,
                                        re_formula = ~ (1 + scale(julian_day) | pred_common_name))) / 100
nd$date <- as.Date(nd$julian_day - 1, origin = paste0(format(dat$date[1], "%Y"), "-01-01"))

ggplot(dat[dat$prop > 0, ], aes(date, prop, fill = pred_common_name, color = pred_common_name)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = n), pch = 21) +
    geom_line(data = nd, aes(y = fit_prop), linewidth = 1.2) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(alpha = 0.6, end = 0.8) +
    scale_color_viridis_d(alpha = 0.8, end = 0.8) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = "Date", y = "Percentage of vocalizations\npredicted as", fill = "Predicted species",
         color = "Predicted species", size = "Number of recorded\nvocalizations") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.5))
```

::: {.alert .alert-info}

#### Summary

- The proportion of focal bellbird vocalizations classified as its own species increased over time (slope `r round(sl3$Slope[sl3$Category == "Three-wattled Bellbird"], 2)` [95% UI: `r round(sl3[["2.5%"]][sl3$Category == "Three-wattled Bellbird"], 2)`–`r round(sl3[["97.5%"]][sl3$Category == "Three-wattled Bellbird"], 2)`])
- The proportions classified as Keel-billed Toucan and Collared Aracari tended to decrease, but their intervals include zero; unassigned vocalizations showed no trend

:::

# Robustness to the hyperparameter configuration

The main results use the selected configuration of each classifier. To check that they do not depend on that choice, the same counts were obtained with each of the configurations compared in the [model fitting](birdnet_model_fitting.qmd) report: focal bellbird clips classified by the 5 fold models of each configuration (ensemble, with that configuration's out-of-fold thresholds), and other bellbirds by its out-of-fold predictions. Configurations whose training diverged were left out.

```{r robustness data}
allp <- read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "predictions_all_configurations.csv"))
# configurations whose training diverged (a classifier that leaves over 90% of clips unassigned,
# never reaching the 0.05 reporting limit in some folds) are left out
unassigned <- tapply(allp$predicted == "Unassigned", list(allp$config, allp$model), mean)
diverged <- rownames(unassigned)[apply(unassigned > 0.9, 1, any)]
allp <- allp[allp$true %in% c("focal", "Procnias tricarunculatus") & !allp$config %in% diverged, ]
rob_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(allp, allp$config), function(d) {
    sa <- d[d$model == "sympatric_and_allopatric", ]
    s <- d[d$model == "sympatric" & d$predicted != "Unassigned", ]
    fs <- sum(sa$true == "focal" & sa$predicted %in% heterosp_sympatric)
    fa <- sum(sa$true == "focal" & sa$predicted %in% allopatric_spp)
    data.frame(config = d$config[1],
               focal_sympatric = fs, focal_allopatric = fa, ratio = fs / fa, share = fs / (fs + fa),
               others_heterospecific = sum(sa$true != "focal" & sa$predicted %in% c(heterosp_sympatric, allopatric_spp)),
               others_total = sum(sa$true != "focal"),
               focal_model_sp = mean(s$predicted[s$true == "focal"] != "Procnias tricarunculatus"),
               others_model_sp = mean(s$predicted[s$true != "focal"] != "Procnias tricarunculatus"))
}))
rob_tab$selected <- ifelse(rob_tab$config == best_cfg[["sympatric_and_allopatric"]] & rob_tab$config == best_cfg[["sympatric"]], "both classifiers",
                    ifelse(rob_tab$config == best_cfg[["sympatric_and_allopatric"]], "sympatric + allopatric",
                    ifelse(rob_tab$config == best_cfg[["sympatric"]], "sympatric only", "")))
```

```{r robustness plot}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4

rl <- rbind(data.frame(config = rob_tab$config, panel = "Sympatric + allopatric classifier:\nfocal heterospecific classifications\nthat are the sympatric species", value = rob_tab$share, bird = "Focal bellbird"),
            data.frame(config = rob_tab$config, panel = "Sympatric-only classifier:\nassigned clips classified\nas a model species", value = rob_tab$focal_model_sp, bird = "Focal bellbird"),
            data.frame(config = rob_tab$config, panel = "Sympatric-only classifier:\nassigned clips classified\nas a model species", value = rob_tab$others_model_sp, bird = "Other bellbirds"))
rl$selected <- rl$config %in% best_cfg

ggplot(rl, aes(bird, value, color = bird)) +
    geom_hline(data = data.frame(panel = unique(rl$panel)[1], y = 0.5), aes(yintercept = y), linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_point(data = rl[rl$selected, ], shape = 21, size = 4, stroke = 1.2, color = "black") +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`Focal bellbird` = "#E07B39", `Other bellbirds` = "#408AB4"), guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(strip.background = element_blank())
```

Each point is one configuration; circled: selected configurations. Dashed line: equal classification as sympatric and allopatric species, expected by chance.

```{r robustness table}
rt <- rob_tab[order(-rob_tab$ratio), ]
kable(data.frame(Configuration = rt$config, Selected = rt$selected,
                 `Focal: sympatric vs allopatric` = paste(rt$focal_sympatric, "vs", rt$focal_allopatric),
                 `Sympatric : allopatric` = round(rt$ratio, 1),
                 `Other bellbirds classified as heterospecific` = paste(rt$others_heterospecific, "of", rt$others_total),
                 `Focal classified as model species (sympatric only)` = scales::percent(rt$focal_model_sp, 0.1),
                 `Others classified as model species (sympatric only)` = scales::percent(rt$others_model_sp, 0.1),
                 check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

::: {.alert .alert-info}

#### Summary

- Across the `r nrow(rob_tab)` hyperparameter configurations whose training converged (`r paste(diverged, collapse = ", ")` diverged and left almost every clip unassigned), `r round(100 * min(rob_tab$share))`–`r round(100 * max(rob_tab$share))`% of the heterospecific classifications of the focal bellbird were the sympatric species (sympatric : allopatric `r round(min(rob_tab$ratio), 1)`–`r round(max(rob_tab$ratio), 1)` : 1), and other bellbirds were classified as a heterospecific in at most `r max(rob_tab$others_heterospecific)` of `r rob_tab$others_total[1]` clips
- With the sympatric-only classifier, `r round(100 * min(rob_tab$focal_model_sp))`–`r round(100 * max(rob_tab$focal_model_sp))`% of the assigned focal bellbird clips were classified as a model species, against at most `r round(100 * max(rob_tab$others_model_sp), 1)`% of other bellbird clips. The conclusions do not depend on the configuration chosen

:::
